summary: Gadolinium nitride films were deposited using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) with tris(methylcyclopentadienyl)gadolinium {Gd(MeCp)3} and remote nitrogen plasma. The films were deposited at temperatures between 150 and 300 1C and were found to have a Gd:N ratio close to 1:1 with low oxygen incorporation. The films were amorphous and showed good uniformity and smoothness.
evidence: Gadolinium nitride films have been deposited on Si(100) using a plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD) based process. The deposition was carried out using tris(methylcyclopentadienyl)gadolinium {Gd(MeCp)3} and remote nitrogen plasma, separated by argon pulses. Films were deposited at temperatures between 150 and 300 1C and capped with tantalum nitride to prevent post-deposition oxidation. Films deposited at 200 1C were found to have a Gd:N ratio close to 1:1 and a low oxygen incorporation ( /C24 5%).
